correctness.rationale: Independently exhausted the 2^18 possible symmetric basis-output tensors. Let L_i be multiplication by e_i and S_i multiplication by e_i^2. In the pointwise defect the coefficient of the reduced function x_i is [S_i,L_i], and that of x_i x_j is [S_i,L_j]+[S_j,L_i]. Evaluating at one- and two-coordinate binary vectors proves their necessity; these are all reduced terms and hence suffice. For extension stability the unreduced terms x_i^2 x_j are distinct and each coordinate degree is at most 3, so separate vanishing is necessary already over F4 by interpolation and is sufficient over every extension. Commutativity makes associativity equivalent to all L_i commuting. The replay python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_nov24_jordan.py uses these operator tests and traverses orbits by two swaps and one involutive elementary addition (they generate GL_3(F2)), rather than testing every product pair and every basis as in the frozen C++ code. It recovered 2858/47, 1898/32 and 988/16 labelled laws/classes, the orbit histogram, stabilizer sums 7896/5376/2688 and the entire byte-identical representative table (SHA-256 b0b9545d04c73a084153374d50f9a3508187f1547c0bf7fcfdb4b7950b53a2e5). For the witness only the e_3 component survives subtraction; it is ab(a+b) times the e_1-coordinate of y, hence zero over F2 and 1 at a=1,b=omega,y=e_1. Associative laws stay associative after extension, so all 15 exceptional orbits are nonassociative. Inspected the frozen checker; only the independent code was executed. No claim about quadratic Jordan structures is verified by this test.
